page: Amazon Web Services r8id.12xlarge is a memory-optimized server powered by an Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor built on the x86_64 architecture. It features 48 vCPUs across 24 physical cores with hyper-threading, operating at a clock speed of 3.9 GHz and supported by a 480 MB L3 cache. The memory configuration consists of 384.0 GB of DDR5 RAM operating at 7 GHz, providing 8.0 GB of memory per core. Local storage is bundled via a 2850 GB NVMe SSD instance store, and networking is supported by a 22 Gbps baseline bandwidth.

Benchmark data indicates strong memory and processing performance. The server achieves top-tier results in Geekbench image and text processing, alongside strong performance in Geekbench single-core, multi-core, and software compilation tests. Memory bandwidth tests show strong read-only performance for both small cached and large uncached blocks, though large block write bandwidth sits in the average tier. Cryptographic and vector operations are accelerated by hardware flags including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions.

With its high memory-to-vCPU ratio and integrated high-speed NVMe SSD storage, the r8id.12xlarge is highly cost-efficient for memory-intensive and I/O-heavy workloads. It demonstrates strong performance in Passmark database operations and Redis SET benchmarks, making it highly suitable for large-scale databases, in-memory caching, and data-intensive applications. Additionally, its strong performance in LLM inference for small and medium models supports localized machine learning tasks without requiring dedicated GPU hardware.

It is equipped with 384.0 GB of high-speed 7 GHz DDR5 memory, a 2850 GB local NVMe SSD instance store, and a 22 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Operating on the Nitro hypervisor, this x86_64 server delivers strong performance across memory bandwidth, database operations, and text processing benchmarks, supported by advanced instruction sets like AVX-512 and Intel AMX. The r8id.12xlarge is highly suited for memory-intensive workloads, including large-scale databases, in-memory caching, and data processing pipelines that benefit from high-speed local storage and dense memory configurations.
